subject: Private VPC networking follow-up / PrivateLink vs VPC peering / IP allowlist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC networking follow-up / PrivateLink vs VPC peering / IP allowlist

Hi Tom —

Thanks for the call this morning — really helpful to understand Acme's security and network requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

Recap
- Use case: customer-facing API for risk-modeling microservice with PII tokenization on ingest.
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC (RDW Private) behind customer VPC with isolated egress and audit logs.
- Key constraints: no public endpoints in prod, strict IP allowlist for outbound to Redwood control plane, and SOC2-compliant audit requirements.

Options we discussed
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, but not acceptable due to your egress/isolation needs.
- Dedicated capacity: could meet isolation and throughput, but still leaves network traffic crossing public internet unless we set up PrivateLink or VPC peering.
- Private VPC (recommended): Redwood runs inference inside your VPC (or in a customer-managed VPC) with PrivateLink or VPC peering + static egress for allowlist.

Open/technical items (ask from your side)
1) Confirm whether your network/security team prefers AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoint) or VPC peering for this workload.
2) Provide the CIDR(s) for any subnets you want Redwood to peer with, and the team contact we should loop in (name + email).
3) Confirm whether Acme requires a fixed set of outbound IPs for our control-plane callbacks (we can provide a small set of static IPs / NAT gateway egress ranges).

Next steps
- I attached our Private VPC networking checklist (redwood-private-vpc-network-checklist.pdf) that lists required SG/ACL entries, route table suggestions, and sample allowlist entries.
- If you prefer, Sean (cc'd) or our infra lead Dev can join a short call with your network team to walk through the checklist and timing.
- Once we have network contact and CIDRs, we’ll produce a mutual action plan (timeline + tasks + deployment window).

Would you be able to share a best point-of-contact for networking and your preferred option (PrivateLink vs peering) by end of week?

Thanks —
Marissa
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-private-vpc-network-checklist.pdf (stub)

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmefinancial.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acmefinancial.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up / PrivateLink vs VPC peering / IP allowlist

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the notes and checklist — appreciate the clarity. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) Preference: Our security team generally prefers PrivateLink for production services because it avoids any cross-account routing changes and fits our current audit model. That said, peering may be OK for a short pilot.
2) Outbound IPs: We do require a static set of egress IPs for allowlisting — can Redwood provide a stable set (or a small CIDR) that won't change during the pilot?
3) Timeline: We’re aiming for a pilot in the next 4–6 weeks if network approvals are quick.

I’ll loop in Sara (network engineering) to coordinate — Sara, can you confirm whether PrivateLink will work for you and share any specific constraints (VPC endpoints, SG rules, required ports)?

Tom
Director of Platform Engineering | Acme Financial
tom.alvarez@acmefinancial.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acmefinancial.com>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC networking follow-up / PrivateLink vs VPC peering / IP allowlist

Tom / Sara —

Thanks — great, PrivateLink is a very common pattern and aligns with our recommended path for production. Quick answers and commitments from our side:

- PrivateLink support: Redwood supports AWS PrivateLink (interface VPC endpoints). We will provide the endpoint service name and the exact port (TLS 443) and SG recommendations.
- Static outbound IPs: For control-plane callbacks and telemetry, we can provide a set of static egress IPs (we run these through a small NAT pool). For the pilot we can reserve and confirm 3 IPs; for production we’ll work with your ops to agree on a stable range.
- Pilot timeline: We can target a 4-week pilot from finalizing network details. Typical pilot tasks: endpoint validation, allowlist confirmation, smoke tests, and 2–3 days of load verification.

Action items I’ve added on our side:
- Dev Patel (cc) will prepare a short tech note with the PrivateLink endpoint service name, recommended SG rules, and example allowlist entries (rdw-allowlist-example.txt).
- I’ll follow up with a short mutual action plan doc and propose two calendar slots next week for a 30m network walkthrough.

Dev — can you prepare the tech note and the allowlist example by Monday 3/16?

Tom / Sara — please confirm the network contact (name + email) we should add to the MAP and whether you prefer PrivateLink or peering for the pilot.

Best,
Marissa
